text:
maria: Hey team — can someone take a quick look at PR #4821? It fixes a subtle race in the batching path when a KV-cache miss hits during stream assembly.

aj: Link? quick summary of the change? :eyes:

maria: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
Summary: keep batcher’s inflight map locked until the KV-prefetch future is swapped in, and add a small backoff when seq_len < 8 to avoid thrashing small requests. Adds unit + integration test.

ravi: skimming now. question: does this change affect the prefix-cache semantics for multi-tenant keys?

maria: good call — it intentionally leaves prefix eviction unchanged, only changes the inflight swap timing. I added a test that simulates concurrent misses across tenants.

aj: I ran the test locally, saw a flaky on the windows CI matrix (timeout in test_batcher_race). try bumping the sleep tolerance or use event wait instead of sleep.

maria: pushed a fix using an Event instead of sleep; forced push to the branch.

sophie: can you share a quick perf run? worried about added latency tail on tiny requests.

maria: micro-bench on A100: median same, p95 +2ms for seq_len<=4, p99 unchanged. I think it's acceptable, left notes in the PR.

aj: CI still running but I can approve after the windows job finishes if deploy-bot reports green.

tim: PTAL from kernel side? if no attention kernel changes I'm fine to approve once tests are green.

maria: there are no kernel edits here, just orchestration. thanks! planning to merge during low-traffic window (tonight 00:30 UTC) and canary to 10% for 30m.

deploy-bot: CI passed: all checks successful (runtime-build, unit-tests, integration-tests, windows-matrix).

aj: +1 — will watch canary.

ravi: thanks for adding the regression test, looks solid.

maria: thanks all — merging after final CI, will post a short follow-up in #eng-runtime when canary starts. :rocket:
